speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The Tripartite Advisory will provide practical guidance to employers on good workplace practices to promote workers’ mental well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: There are existing programmes and resources that employers can tap on to help them implement mental wellness programmes at the workplace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For instance, HPB provides Management Training workshops to equip managers and HR professionals with knowledge and skills to be supportive leaders at the workplace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Companies can also tap on HPB's Workplace Outreach Wellness or WOW Package to co-fund and implement health promotion programmes, such as mental wellness workshops for their staff.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: There is also the iWorkHealth online self-assessment tool developed by MOM, IMH, HPB, Workplace Safety and Health Council and CGH to help companies identify common workplace stressors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: There are also many community resources in place to support individual workers who need emotional and psychological help.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Various agencies, such as NCSS, the Agency for Integrated Care or AIC, and MSF work with social service agencies to provide services, such as counselling and mental health resources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For example, NCSS funds the Singapore Anglican Community Services to provide training and advisory support to employers and co-workers in creating an inclusive and supportive work environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: NCSS also organises a multi-year public education campaign called Beyond the Label to address stigma faced by persons living with mental health conditions in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This year's campaign encourages working adults who are affected by mental health distress to seek mental health support early.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We are also encouraged to note that companies have stepped forward to take action in promoting workplace mental health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For instance, the WorkWell Leaders network organises regular meetings among corporate leaders to discuss ways to improve workplace mental health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: NCSS also has a Peer Support Specialist Programme that trains individuals who have recovered from mental health issues as Peer Support Specialists to support others in their recovery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: MOM will continue to work with our partners to educate and gain the support of employers to further promote workers' mental well-being at the workplace.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I am certainly heartened by the measures and programmes that are available for mental health at the workplaces.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: So, my question will be, will these progammes and measures be made mandatory across all workplaces.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: And my second is, if these programmes are in place, will MOM conduct regular studies on the efficacy of the programmes so that we can better understand and use these programmes to help our workers?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: First, whether these programmes will be made mandatory.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On whether to make it mandatory, I think the challenge would be that every workplace is different.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Under the Act alone, there are certain obligation when employers will take care of their workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And therefore, to some extent, there is safeguards in place to ensure that employers take this quite seriously.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On the Member's second point, whether we will measure this, certainly, every programme has got its objectives, targets, goals and KPIs and the various agencies, I am sure, will track the efficacy of each individual programme.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But for us to track every single mental health issue at the workplace, this would be quite challenging, for example, trying to track MCs, how do you do that for individual workplaces?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The second challenge would be this: when you deal with mental health, the root cause may not necessarily be from the workplace too.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: You do need to ascertain that the root causes are at work and whether we can deal with it better at work, for example.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These are some of the measures that we can take at the workplace.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is an evolving area in which I think many of us, whether it is Government, whether it is the employers, are closely monitoring, given the fact that we do have to better understand the workplace stressors that our employees face, and especially today, under COVID-19 conditions.
